newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay truckers defiant as strike ends across India.
newsitem.headline: Bombay truckers defiant as strike ends across India.

text.p: Truckers in India's western state of Maharashtra on Thursday said they were continuing a 10 day-old strike despite a decision by unions in other parts of the country to call off the nationwide action.
"We are continuing the strike and want the state government to accept our main demands," a spokesman for the state's main federation of truckers unions told Reuters.

Spokesman Dayanand Natkar of the Maharashtra Rajya Truck Tempo Tankers Bus Mahasangh, which represents 180 unions totalling about 200,000 members, said they wanted an increase in state motor vehicle and sales taxes withdrawn, as well as other smaller demands.
Maharashtra is India's commercial centre. The state's capital Bombay is the country's busiest port.

On Wednesday, India's truck owners agreed to end the strike, a senior government official said. The transport stoppage, which took 2.2 million vehicles off the roads, has hit the economy hard by paralysing the transport of essential commodities, leading to soaring prices.
"The strike is over," a Surface Transport Ministry official said on Wednesday. "They agreed. We agreed. That's all."

In New Delhi, S.P. Singh, spokesman for the All India Motor Transport Congress (AIMTC), the truckers' union, said the government had agreed to free truck owners from having to collect a five percent service tax and also agreed to hold off on a hike in insurance premiums.
Indian truckers had launched the strike to protest against the service tax and insurance premium hike, which were proposed by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his February 28 budget.
S.V. Damankar, secretary of the Bombay Port Trust, said cargo handling had fallen off to 3,000 tonnes a day compared with the usual 250,000 tonnes.
Analysts said businesses that depended on agricultural produce were the worst hit by the truck strike.
"The economy is losing at least 70 billion to 80 billion rupees ($1.9 billion to $2.2 billion) per day," K.R. Vishwanathan, a senior economist at the Birla Economic Research Foundation, told Reuters.
Maharashtra's Natkar said the federation of truck unions would meet the state transport secretary later on Thursday in a bid to resolve the crisis.
"If the demands are met, we will call off the strike," he said. State government officials were not immediately available for comment.
